title: Detection of autoantibodies with self-assembling radiolabeled antigen tetramers
protocol: Design and generate antigen-streptavidin fusion constructs using established PCR protocols with Pfu polymerase.
Connect the antigen of interest to a monomer of streptavidin using a flexible methionine-rich linker sequence.
Ligate the antigen-streptavidin fusion sequence into the multiple cloning site of a vector containing the SP6 promoter and transform _E. coli_.
Verify that the sequence and orientation of the insert are correct in transformed _E. coli_.
Grow an overnight culture of transformed _E. coli_.
Prepare plasmid DNA by midiprep according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Use the RiboMax SP6 RNA production kit to prepare mRNA according to the manufacturers' instructions.
Purify mRNA using the RNeasy purification kit.
Aliquot mRNA and store at -80°C.
Calculate the number of reactions needed for planned immunoprecipitation \(IP) reactions plus two additional reactions for input and negative control IP with no serum.
Translate each antigen independently if combining multiple antigens in a single IP.
Calculate the amount of each reaction component needed for in vitro translation for each mRNA construct used.
Thaw reticulocyte lysate and ER microsomal membranes on ice.
Thaw RNAse inhibitor, amino acids minus Met and Cys, biotin, ProMix, and RNA at 37°C and spin down.
Combine RNA and water, heat at 70°C for 2 minutes to denature secondary structures.
Snap-cool the RNA on ice and spin down.
Add remaining components to diluted RNA in the order listed and mix well.
For large-scale translations, split IVT into multiple tubes, each with no more than 200 μL.
Translate in a 30°C water bath for 1 hour.
Transition the reaction to oxidizing conditions by adding oxidized glutathione to a final concentration of 4 mM.
Incubate at 30°C for 2 hours.
Add 800 μL of cold RIA stopping buffer.
Centrifuge at full speed for 10 minutes at 4°C to pellet membranes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 50 μL of stopping buffer.
Wash again with 1 mL of stopping buffer.
After washing, remove all supernatant from membrane fraction.
Add solubilization buffer (5 μL per IP reaction or 2.5 μL per IP per antigen if combining two antigens or using an internal control).
Resuspend the membranes by scraping the pipette tip against the sides of the tube and gently pipetting up and down.
Vortex the tubes at the lowest speed for at least 30 minutes to permeabilize membranes.
Centrifuge the permeabilized membranes for 1 minute.
Add the supernatant to the top of a Spin-X filter tube.
Centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute to remove insoluble material.
(Optional) Add DTT to 10 mM to reduce disulfide bonds and SDS to 0.5% to prevent aggregation.
Place a locking cap on the top of the tube.
Heat at 70°C for 15 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, spin down, and then filter the antigen in a Spin-X tube to remove any aggregates.
If combining antigens of different molecular weights or using an internal IP control, mix the antigens together at this time.
Remove 5 μL of antigen and store at 4°C (or freeze) as a reference for the initial amount of radioactivity in each IP reaction.
Combine the remaining solubilized antigen with RIA buffer and Protein A-Sepharose beads for pre-clearing.
Incubate at 4 °C on an orbital rotator for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Add cleared antigen and beads to the top of a Spin-X filter.
Centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute to remove beads.
Confirm the final volume and add buffer as needed to replace bead volume.
Place 200 μL of RIA buffer in each IP tube.
Add serum (2.5 μL for final dilution of 1:100).
Add 50 μL of cleared antigen.
If performing parallel reactions with folded and denatured tetramers, add DTT to a final concentration of 220 μM in IP reactions with folded tetramers.
Place IP reactions on an orbital rotator.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Add 20 μL of blocked 50% Protein A-Sepharose beads to each tube.
Place on an orbital rotator at 4 °C for 90 minutes to precipitate immunoglobulins and bound antigen.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL of cold RIA buffer.
Pulse-centrifuge to pellet beads, and carefully remove most supernatant with a pipette.
Add 10 μL of CAPS buffer to elute immunoglobulins.
Vortex tubes at low speed for 15-20 minutes at 4°C.
Prepare fresh gel loading buffer.
For deglycosylation, add 1,000 units of EndoH per reaction.
Place 10 μL of buffer in the bottom of a Spin-X tube for each sample.
Spin down IP tubes to settle beads.
Remove all of the beads and buffer with a wide bore pipette tip, and transfer to the top of a prepared Spin-X filter tube.
Centrifuge 1 min at full speed to remove beads.
Add 10 μL of gel loading buffer to the "input" reaction.
Vortex all tubes briefly to mix buffer.
If digesting with EndoH, incubate tubes at 37°C for two hours.
Load samples onto SDS-PAGE gels.
Include one lane of prestained molecular weight markers to orient the gel on the transfer membrane.
Run gels at the appropriate voltage and time for the gel system in use.
Equilibrate a piece of PVDF membrane in 100% methanol until it turns translucent.
Transfer the equilibrated PVDF membrane to a tray of distilled water and allow it to equilibrate for at least 5 minutes, occasionally tapping the tray gently.

Transfer proteins from the gel to a PVDF membrane using transfer cassettes assembled in the following order: back of cassette, fiber pad, piece of Whatman paper, wetted PVDF membrane, gel, piece of Whatman paper, fiber pad, front of cassette. Avoid trapping bubbles between layers.
Place the assembly in the transfer apparatus and add an ice block to prevent overheating. Transfer at 100 V for 1 hour in a cold room or at 30 V overnight.

Remove the membrane from the transfer apparatus and allow it to dry completely by placing it on Whatman paper in the flow path of a laminar flow hood for 20 minutes or leave it on the benchtop overnight.
Clear a storage phosphor screen by exposing it to light while the membrane is drying.
Place dried membranes in Phosphor exposure cassette.
Expose overnight.
Acquire data on Phosphor Imager.
Draw a line down each lane of the gel.
Calculate the area of all peaks along that density line.
Export an image of the gels.
Save peak quantifications to Excel.
Use the peak(s) specific for the protein(s) of interest to analyze the data.
Divide the area of the antigen-specific peaks from each immunoprecipitation reaction by the peak area of each antigen in the "input" lane.
Set a threshold of reactivity above which a sample is considered positive.
Adjust brightness and contrast to make all protein bands visible.
